userStories.title: Add manifest retention configuration and purge module
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add opt-in manifest-retention configuration and an age-based purge module that bounds Context Engine v2 manifest growth.

**Motivation** — `src/context/engine/manifest-store.ts` has no prune, retention, or TTL path of any kind — manifests accumulate for the life of the repository.

**Approach** — Retention is **age-based on file mtime**, not keep-newest-N. `ContextManifest` carries no timestamp field of its own, so mtime is the only available age signal; a keep-newest-N policy would need mtime anyway to rank recency, making it strictly more machinery for the same input. Age also matches the mental model operators already have from `context.v2.session.retentionDays`.

The sweep covers **all** feature directories, not just the feature being run. This is a deliberate divergence from `purgeStaleScratch()`, which is scoped to a single feature. Per-feature scoping cannot bound growth: a run touches one feature, so the other 70 feature directories observed on this repo would never be swept.

Discovery uses one capped glob rather than a nested directory walk, scanned relative to `projectDir`:

```
.nax/features/*/stories/*/{context-manifest-*,rebuild-manifest}.json
```

For each match: read its mtime, and delete it when `mtimeMs < now - retentionDays * 86_400_000`. After processing a story directory, attempt a **non-recursive** directory removal on it. Non-recursive removal is the safety property that matters here: it fails harmlessly when any non-manifest artifact remains, so no recursive deletion is ever performed against a path built from feature and story names.

Following `.nax/rules/project-conventions.md` and `forbidden-patterns-source.md`, the module exposes an injectable `_manifestPurgeDeps` object (`now`, `scan`, `statMtime`, `unlink`, `rmdirIfEmpty`) — `mock.module()` is banned in this codebase, so dependency injection is the only testable seam. Glob scans pass `cwd` explicitly and are capped, per `monorepo-awareness.md` §6.

**Scope** — In: add the optional `context.v2.manifest.retentionDays` schema and runtime field; create the purge module; scan every feature's manifest paths with the specified cap; preserve unreadable files; and safely attempt non-recursive cleanup of story directories. Out: wiring `handleRunCompletion` to invoke the purge (US-002); modifying `manifest-store.ts`; whole feature-directory retention — `prd.json`, `plan/`, `checkpoint.jsonl`, `status.json` and acceptance artifacts are not pruned by this feature, which touches context manifests only; archiving manifests to an `_archive/` directory instead of deleting them; and a keep-newest-N retention policy.

**Interface**
```typescript
// src/context/engine/manifest-purge.ts
export async function purgeStaleManifests(
  projectDir: string,
  retentionDays: number,
): Promise<number>;
```

Config schema: add a `manifest` block to `ContextV2ConfigSchema` in `src/config/schemas-context.ts:114`, mirroring the `session` block at `:164-171` — but with `.optional()` and **no** `.default()`, so an unset key resolves to `undefined`. Because Zod omits an optional-without-default key entirely, `DEFAULT_CONFIG` keeps its current shape and no existing config assertion changes. Runtime type: add the matching optional `manifest` field to `ContextV2Config` in `src/config/runtime-types-context.ts:85`, mirroring the `session` type at `:112-118`. Barrel: export `purgeStaleManifests` from `src/context/engine/index.ts`.
acceptanceCriteria: [ContextV2ConfigSchema.parse] returns a configuration whose manifest is undefined when parsing an empty configuration object.
[ContextV2ConfigSchema.parse] returns context.v2.manifest.retentionDays equal to 30 when parsing a configuration that sets that field to 30.
[ContextV2ConfigSchema.parse] throws schema validation when context.v2.manifest.retentionDays is 0.
[purgeStaleManifests] returns 0 when the project directory contains no .nax/features directory.
[purgeStaleManifests] deletes a context-manifest-context.json file whose mtime is 31 days old when retentionDays is 30.
[purgeStaleManifests] leaves a context-manifest-context.json file present when its mtime is 29 days old and retentionDays is 30.
[purgeStaleManifests] returns the number of manifest files it deleted.
[purgeStaleManifests] deletes a rebuild-manifest.json file whose mtime is 31 days old when retentionDays is 30.
When the injected statMtime lookup throws for a manifest, then purgeStaleManifests leaves that file on disk.
When the injected statMtime lookup throws for a manifest, then purgeStaleManifests excludes that file from its returned deletion count.
When purgeStaleManifests deletes the last manifest in a story directory, then that story directory no longer exists.
When a story directory contains a file that is neither a context manifest nor a rebuild manifest, then purgeStaleManifests leaves both the directory and that file in place.
When purgeStaleManifests reaches MAX_MANIFEST_SCAN entries, then it stops examining entries and emits a debug-level log naming MAX_MANIFEST_SCAN.

routing.reasoning: The story adds one bounded filesystem module plus established config and barrel updates, with safety-sensitive retention behavior but no new cross-system abstraction.

outOfScope: Wire the manifest purge into run completion; that belongs to US-002.

userStories.title: Run manifest retention during completion
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Invoke the opt-in manifest retention sweep from run completion without allowing housekeeping failures to fail the run.

**Motivation** — Session scratch already solved the same problem next door: `context.v2.session.retentionDays` drives `purgeStaleScratch()` from `run-completion.ts`. Manifests were simply never given the equivalent.

**Approach** — Call site: `handleRunCompletion()` in `src/execution/lifecycle/run-completion.ts:110`, immediately after the existing scratch-purge block at `:460-479`, gated by `if (manifestCfg?.retentionDays)` — the identical truthiness idiom that gates the scratch purge at `:463`.

**Scope** — In: import and invoke `purgeStaleManifests` through the injectable completion dependency seam after session scratch retention; use the resolved project directory and configured retention days; log positive deletions at info; and catch rejection at warn level while preserving normal completion. Out: defining the config key and implementing the sweep (US-001); changing session scratch retention; emitting a retention-knob advertisement when it is unset; adding concurrency safety; or adding a manual CLI purge command.

**Interface**
```typescript
export async function purgeStaleManifests(
  projectDir: string,
  retentionDays: number,
): Promise<number>;
```

Failure handling: `purgeStaleManifests` rejection is fail-open — `handleRunCompletion` logs at warn level and completes normally. A retention sweep never fails a run.

**File-size constraint:** `run-completion.ts` is at **549 lines** against the repo's 600-line hard limit (`bun run check:file-sizes`). The new block must stay small; if it would breach 600, extract it rather than growing the file.
acceptanceCriteria: Given context.v2.manifest.retentionDays is 30, when handleRunCompletion runs, then it invokes purgeStaleManifests exactly once with the resolved project directory and 30.
Given context.v2.manifest is unset, when handleRunCompletion runs, then it does not invoke purgeStaleManifests.
Given purgeStaleManifests rejects, when handleRunCompletion runs with manifest retention configured, then handleRunCompletion resolves with its normal completion result.
Given purgeStaleManifests rejects, when handleRunCompletion runs with manifest retention configured, then it emits a warn-level log recording the failure.
Given purgeStaleManifests returns a count greater than zero, when handleRunCompletion runs, then it emits an info-level log carrying that count.

routing.reasoning: This is a small but convention-sensitive lifecycle integration that must preserve completion semantics, logging behavior, test injection, and the source-file size limit.

outOfScope: Define the config key and purge algorithm; that belongs to US-001.

analysis: This is an additive Context Engine v2 retention enhancement, not a greenfield feature. `src/context/engine/manifest-store.ts:44-54` establishes the target layout as `<projectDir>/.nax/features/<featureId>/stories/<storyId>/` with `context-manifest-<stage>.json` and `rebuild-manifest.json`; it must remain unmodified. `src/session/scratch-purge.ts:17-41,53-95` is the direct retention-module precedent: an exported injectable dependency object, injected clock, bounded age calculation using `86_400_000`, fail-safe discovery, and a numeric purge count. The new module should use its own `_manifestPurgeDeps` (`now`, `scan`, `statMtime`, `unlink`, `rmdirIfEmpty`) to permit tests without banned `mock.module()`. Its scan must be a capped Bun glob with explicit `cwd: projectDir`, using `.nax/features/*/stories/*/{context-manifest-*,rebuild-manifest}.json`; it needs to process all features rather than only the current feature so old manifest growth is actually bounded. A stat failure must retain and not count that path. Once a story directory has been processed, it must only attempt non-recursive removal, preserving any directory that retains a non-manifest artifact. Missing `.nax/features` must be a zero-result, and cap exhaustion must generate a debug record naming `MAX_MANIFEST_SCAN`. `src/config/schemas-context.ts:114-254` has `ContextV2ConfigSchema`: add an optional `manifest` object alongside its defaulted `session` object, with `retentionDays: z.number().int().min(1)` and no object or field default. This preserves `DEFAULT_CONFIG`'s current shape and makes `ContextV2ConfigSchema.parse({}).manifest` undefined; through `ContextConfigSchema`, that is `context.v2.manifest`. `src/config/runtime-types-context.ts:85-141` must expose the matching optional runtime field. `src/context/engine/index.ts:58-65` is the public barrel location for the new export. `src/execution/lifecycle/run-completion.ts:20-39` imports scratch retention and exposes `_runCompletionDeps`, while `:460-479` calculates `effectiveProjectDir`, gates the sibling purge by truthiness, logs a positive purge count at info, and catches errors at warn level. Add the manifest call immediately after that block, gated with `if (manifestCfg?.retentionDays)`, routed through the injectable completion dependency seam so the integration test can stub it. The sweep is best-effort: a rejection must not alter the normal completion result. `run-completion.ts` is currently 549 lines, below the 600-line hard limit, so the new block must stay small or be extracted if it grows too far. Existing coverage patterns are `test/unit/session/scratch-purge.test.ts` for injectable retention behavior and `test/unit/execution/lifecycle-completion.test.ts` plus `test/unit/execution/lifecycle/run-completion-*.test.ts` for `handleRunCompletion`; add focused tests without using module mocks. Backward compatibility is intentional: absent config means no purge and no newly defaulted config state, preserving existing `nax context inspect` history. There is no data migration: operators opt in by setting `context.v2.manifest.retentionDays`; enabling it irreversibly removes only manifests older than the configured mtime cutoff. Main risks are path safety (never recursively remove a path derived from feature/story names), accidental pruning after stat errors, unbounded scans, and allowing housekeeping errors to fail completed runs.
outOfScope: Whole feature-directory retention — `prd.json`, `plan/`, `checkpoint.jsonl`, `status.json` and acceptance artifacts are not pruned by this feature, which touches context manifests only.
Archiving manifests to an `_archive/` directory instead of deleting them; the sweep deletes only.
Curator rollup garbage collection (issue #1445) is unchanged by this feature.
A keep-newest-N retention policy; retention is age-based on file mtime only.
Session scratch retention is unchanged — `purgeStaleScratch()` and the `context.v2.session` config keep their existing behaviour.
A log message advertising the retention knob when it is unset.

Concurrency safety of any kind: neither a second nax process purging the same directories, nor a concurrent reader such as `nax context inspect` or `loadContextManifests` observing a directory mid-purge, is addressed. The sweep runs at run completion and is best-effort.

Retention of manifests belonging to a feature that is still in progress is not treated specially — age is the only criterion, so a long-running feature's early manifests are eligible for deletion like any other.
A CLI command to trigger the manifest purge manually.
